Definition: from G1344; an equitable deed; by implication, a statute or decision:--judgment, justification, ordinance, righteousness.
BiblicalUsage: A dikaioma is a righteous deed or a just decree, sometimes the ordinance itself and sometimes the right act it requires. Zacharias and Elisabeth walked in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless, and Paul sets one man's righteous act against Adam's offence. In Revelation the fine linen of the bride is the righteous acts of the saints.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God's righteous requirements are not a ladder I climb to earn His favour. Christ's one righteous act did what I never could, and now my own righteous deeds are the fruit of His work, not the price of it.
